answers.label: Q.1(a)
answers.finalAnswer: Anything that disturbs his balance because it stops him from getting what he wants, or anything that causes him difficulty or makes a situation worse.
answers.solution: To a common man, a problem is anything that disturbs his equilibrium (peace of mind) because it prevents him from achieving something he wants. It can also be anything that causes him difficulty or makes (compounds) a situation more complicated for him.

answers.label: Q.1(b)
answers.finalAnswer: By managing our time well, respecting our elders, showing kindness to others and loving nature.
answers.solution:
Many of our problems will disappear if we:
1. manage our time well,
2. respect our elders (listen to our parents),
3. show kindness to others, and
4. love and take care of nature.

answers.label: Q.1(c)
answers.finalAnswer: Personal problem: a student cannot find his pencil; global problem: a pandemic.
answers.solution:
Personal problem: a student who cannot find his pencil (or a family whose roof is damaged by hailstones).
Global problem: a pandemic, which affects the entire world (the passage mentions a Prime Minister trying to find a way to overcome the pandemic).

answers.label: Q.1(d)
answers.finalAnswer: As an opportunity to test oneself, learn lessons of life and become a better version of oneself.
answers.solution: For someone who loves to face problems, a problem is not a trouble but an opportunity to test himself. Such people believe that these situations teach them many lessons of life and finally help them become better versions of themselves.

answers.label: Q.1(e)
answers.finalAnswer: Problems are a part of everyone's life; many are created by ourselves and can be avoided by good habits, and the rest should be faced as chances to learn and grow.
answers.solution: After reading the passage, I conclude that no one is free from problems; they are a normal part of life. Many of our problems are created by us and can be avoided by managing time, respecting elders, being kind and caring for nature. The problems that remain should not frighten us. We should face them bravely as opportunities to learn and become better people.

answers.label: Q.1(f)
answers.finalAnswer: (iv) Problems are not helpful at all.
answers.solution: (iv) 'Problems are not helpful at all' is not true. The passage says that some people see problems as opportunities that teach them lessons of life and help them become better versions of themselves, so problems can be helpful.

answers.label: Q.1(g)
answers.finalAnswer: (i) utopian; (ii) compounds
answers.solution:
(i) Ideal: utopian ('we do not live in a utopian world').
(ii) Complicate: compounds ('compounds a situation for him').

answers.label: Q.1(h)
answers.finalAnswer: (i) absorbed in (our work); (ii) hunky dory
answers.solution:
(i) Concentrate: 'absorbed in' ('When we are absorbed in our work').
(ii) There is no problem: 'hunky dory' ('everything is hunky dory', meaning everything is fine).

answers.label: Q.2(a)
answers.finalAnswer: The robes of a new-born child (blue in colour).
answers.solution: In the early morning (at break of day) the weavers weave the robes of a new-born child, blue as the wing of a wild bluebird.

answers.label: Q.2(b)
answers.finalAnswer: marriage veil of a queen
answers.solution: The marriage veil of a queen is purple and green coloured. The weavers weave it at fall of night, bright 'like the plumes of a peacock, purple or green'.

answers.label: Q.2(c)
answers.finalAnswer: The weavers (Indian weavers).
answers.solution: The poet addresses the Indian weavers, asking them what they weave at different times of the day.

answers.label: Q.2(d)
answers.finalAnswer: The weavers, solemn and still, weave a white funeral shroud for a dead man.
answers.solution: In the chilly moonlight the weavers sit solemn and still and weave a dead man's funeral shroud, white as a feather and white as a cloud.

answers.label: Q.2(e)
answers.finalAnswer: birth, youth (marriage) and death
answers.solution: The three stages of life mentioned in the poem are birth (the robes of a new-born child), youth or marriage (the marriage veils of a queen) and death (a dead man's funeral shroud).

answers.label: Q.3
answers.solution:
12, Rajpur Road
Dehradun
15 June 2021

The Editor
The Times of India
New Delhi

Subject: Being ready for a future pandemic

Sir,

Through your newspaper, I wish to suggest how our nation can deal with another pandemic in future.

COVID-19 caught us unprepared. First, every district must have well-equipped hospitals with enough beds, oxygen and trained staff. Second, people should follow good habits even in normal times: washing hands, wearing masks in crowds and eating healthy food. Third, schools and offices must be ready to shift online quickly, so that learning and work do not stop. Fourth, the government should keep a store of medicines and vaccines and share correct information, so that rumours do not spread panic. Finally, we must help the poor and the elderly, who suffer most in such times.

If we prepare now, we can face the next pandemic with courage.

Yours faithfully,
Arjun Singh

answers.label: Q.4
answers.solution:
Title: Kinds of Students

Students are usually grouped as good, naughty and weak. Good students are intelligent, obedient, punctual and modest. Naughty students, though often clever, disturb the class, quarrel and may even steal. Weak students do poorly in exams because they do not understand their lessons, owing to a poor foundation or a lack of confidence, motivation or guidance. Teachers and parents must work together to find the cause, motivate such students, clear their doubts and help them set realistic goals.

(about 80 words, against about 180 in the original)

answers.label: Q.5
answers.solution:
My Favourite Dream

When night comes down and stars appear,
I close my eyes and lose my fear.
A dream comes softly, bright and clear,
The one I love throughout the year.

I wear a cadet's uniform with pride,
My friends are marching by my side.
The drums are beating, loud and wide,
And flags are waving far and wide.

I fly a jet above the land,
The mountains look like grains of sand.
I guard my country, firm I stand,
With courage strong and steady hand.

Then morning comes, the dream must end,
But I will work, my dream to tend.
On hard work only I depend,
To make my dream come true, my friend.

answers.label: Q.6
answers.solution:
Effect of the Pandemic on the Education of School-going Children
By Arjun Singh, Class VII

In March 2020, schools across India suddenly shut their gates because of the COVID-19 pandemic. Classrooms fell silent, and for nearly two years children studied from home. This changed school education in many ways.

The biggest change was online learning. Classes moved to mobile phones and laptops. Students learnt to use video calls, online tests and digital notes. Many children became good at using technology, and some discovered they could learn on their own.

However, the harm was greater. Millions of children in villages and poor families had no smartphone or internet connection, so they could not attend classes at all. Many fell behind, and some left school to help their families earn money. Even those who studied online found it hard to concentrate for hours in front of a small screen. Long screen time caused headaches, eye strain and poor sleep.

Children also missed the joys of school life: playing with friends, sports, assemblies and talking face to face with teachers. Many felt lonely, bored or anxious. Teachers say that young children lost basic reading and writing skills, and older students forgot much of what they had learnt.

Now that schools have reopened, we must help children catch up. Extra classes, remedial teaching and counselling can fill the gaps. The government should also make sure every child has access to digital devices, so that no child is left behind if schools ever have to close again.

The pandemic taught us that a school is not only a place to study, but also a place to grow.

answers.label: Q.7
answers.solution:
Best Friends Forever

Every evening, little Riya and her golden dog Bruno walked down the shady path behind their house. Tall ferns grew on both sides, and the trees whispered in the breeze. Bruno wagged his fluffy tail and never left Riya's side.

One evening Riya walked too far and the sky grew dark. She could not find the way back and began to cry. Bruno licked her hand, sniffed the ground and gently pulled at her sleeve. Riya held on to his soft fur and followed him.

Step by step, Bruno led her along the path until the lights of her house appeared. Her worried parents ran out and hugged her tightly. That night Riya gave Bruno an extra biscuit and whispered, 'You are my best friend forever.'

(about 125 words)

answers.label: Q.8
answers.finalAnswer: He refused to accept the award with dignity.; Having scored the highest runs in the match, he was adjudged man of the match.; He is so young that he cannot understand the situation.; He was late but he was not punished.; Jaipur is more beautiful than most other cities in India.; The two girls said that the show should begin.; My mother said to them, "I have not received my son's letter."; cannot be changed (intransitive verb); Give each student a pen after the assembly.; He followed his advice unhesitatingly.
answers.solution:
(a) He refused to accept the award with dignity.
(b) Having scored the highest runs in the match, he was adjudged man of the match.
(c) He is so young that he cannot understand the situation.
(d) He was late but he was not punished.
(e) Jaipur is more beautiful than most other cities in India.
(f) The two girls said that the show should begin. (A 'Let' sentence that expresses a wish becomes 'said that ... should'.)
(g) My mother said to them, "I have not received my son's letter." (In the direct speech the mother speaks, so 'my letter' becomes 'my son's letter' or 'his letter'; the past perfect 'had not received' becomes the present perfect.)
(h) This sentence cannot be changed into the passive voice. 'Come' is an intransitive verb and has no object, so there is nothing to become the subject of a passive sentence.
(i) Give each student a pen after the assembly.
(j) He followed his advice unhesitatingly. ('readily' is also correct.)
(Part (h), as printed, asks for something that is not possible, so it is answered by saying why.)

answers.label: Q.9
answers.finalAnswer: dream; organ; mango; garden; danger
answers.solution:
ARMAGEDON has the letters A, R, M, A, G, E, D, O, N. Five words of four or more letters, each with no letter repeated:
1. DREAM: My dream is to become an officer in the Indian Army.
2. ORGAN: The heart is the organ that pumps blood through the body.
3. MANGO: The mango is called the king of fruits.
4. GARDEN: My grandfather grows roses in his garden.
5. DANGER: The soldiers were ready to face any danger.
(Other correct words: RANGE, GRAND, ROAM, DRAGON, MODERN, ANGER.)
(The printed word is a misspelling of ARMAGEDDON, which has two D's; this does not affect the words above.)

answers.label: Q.10
answers.finalAnswer: He that would eat the fruit must climb the tree.; I will be very happy should he come home in time.; Walk carefully lest you should fall.; My brother came home after I had finished the work.; Only when I read the newspaper did I know that he won the match.; Before the advent of the internet, we wrote letters by hand.; We waited eagerly for the postman to deliver one.; Those were the days of epic drama television serials.; Television then meant just one channel.; Cassette and video recorders were still in vogue.
answers.solution:
(a) He that would eat the fruit must climb the tree.
(b) I will be very happy should he come home in time. (Also: Should he come home in time, I will be very happy.)
(c) Walk carefully lest you should fall.
(d) My brother came home after I had finished the work.
(e) Only when I read the newspaper did I know that he won the match.
(f) Before the advent of the internet, we wrote letters by hand.
(g) We waited eagerly for the postman to deliver one.
(h) Those were the days of epic drama television serials.
(i) Television then meant just one channel.
(j) Cassette and video recorders were still in vogue.
(As printed, (e) gives 'know' twice and 'I' only once, but the sensible sentence needs 'I' twice and 'know' once; it is answered in that sensible form.)

answers.label: Q.12
answers.finalAnswer: (ii) rigorous; (iv) uncontrollably wild; (iii) to imitate; (ii) puzzling; (i) rise and float in air
answers.solution:
(a) AUSTERE: (ii) rigorous (strict and severe).
(b) BERSERK: (iv) uncontrollably wild.
(c) EMULATE: (iii) to imitate (to copy someone you admire in order to equal them).
(d) ENIGMATIC: (ii) puzzling.

answers.label: Q.13
answers.finalAnswer: a bad egg / put all your eggs in one basket; pull someone's leg / not have a leg to stand on; kill two birds with one stone / a bird's eye view; see eye to eye / turn a blind eye; Achilles' heel / take to one's heels
answers.solution:
(a) Egg: a bad egg (a dishonest person); put all your eggs in one basket (depend on one thing only).
(b) Leg: pull someone's leg (tease someone); not have a leg to stand on (have no support for one's argument).
(c) Bird: kill two birds with one stone (do two things with one action); a bird's eye view (a view from high above).
(d) Eyes: see eye to eye (agree completely); turn a blind eye (pretend not to notice).
(e) Heel: Achilles' heel (a weak point); take to one's heels (run away).

answers.label: Q.15
answers.finalAnswer: are; is; has; was; are; are; likes; were; are; is
answers.solution:
(a) are: 'a number of' means many, so the verb is plural.
(b) is: 'dal and rice' is one dish.
(c) has: 'sugar' is uncountable.
(d) was: 'income' is uncountable.
(e) are: 'police' always takes a plural verb.
(f) are: with 'neither ... nor' the verb agrees with the nearer subject, 'the two students'.
(g) likes: the subject is 'one'.
(h) were: an imaginary condition takes 'were'.
(i) are: two subjects joined by 'and'.
(j) is: with 'as well as' the verb agrees with the first subject, 'Aman'.
